summary: Children convert between units of time — hours↔minutes, minutes↔seconds, years↔months, weeks↔days — including mixed quantities (e.g. 3 hours 25 minutes = 3×60 + 25 = 205 minutes). The core idea is MULTIPLICATIVE conversion (×60, ×7, ×12) using known number facts, and resisting the base-10 pull that wrongly assumes 100 seconds in a minute or 100 minutes in an hour. Reverse conversions require dividing and expressing the remainder (150 s → 2 min 30 s). Documented errors are additive rather than multiplicative reasoning, base-10 assumptions, mishandling the remainder/second unit in mixed quantities, and treating every month as exactly 4 weeks.
misconceptions: Uses additive reasoning instead of multiplicative for conversions
Assumes base-10 (100 seconds in a minute, 100 minutes in an hour)
Thinks every month is exactly 4 weeks / all months are the same length
Converts a mixed quantity by ignoring the remainder or the second unit

activities.title: Multiply-then-combine with a conversion machine
steps: Take a mixed quantity such as 3 hours 25 minutes and convert it: multiply the whole units by the rate (3 × 60 = 180 minutes), then add the remaining 25 to get 205 minutes.
State out loud whether you counted up or multiplied, and why multiplying is faster.
Work a reverse conversion: take 150 seconds, group it into sixties — two full groups of 60 make 2 minutes, with 30 seconds left over, giving '2 minutes 30 seconds'.
Test the tempting '100 to a minute' idea against grouping real seconds into sixties, and describe what goes wrong.
activities.insight: Converting units of time is multiply (by the fixed rate) then combine the remainder — not counting up — and for seconds, minutes and hours the grouping is 60, not 100.

activities.title: Known-facts conversion with a base-10 trap item
steps: Fill in conversions such as '3 h 25 min = ___ min' and show the multiply-then-add working.
Match a seconds amount (e.g. 150 s) to its minutes-and-seconds form.
Choose the correct reading of 150 seconds and explain why '1.5 minutes' (base-10 thinking) and '2 minutes' (dropped remainder) are both wrong.
Convert 8 weeks 3 days to days using 8 × 7 = 56, then + 3 = 59 days.
activities.insight: Secure conversions rest on known multiplication facts and on keeping the remainder; the common wrong answers to the 150-seconds item — '1.5 minutes' and '2 minutes' — correspond to base-10 thinking and to dropping the remainder.

activities.title: Irregular units: months, weeks and the calendar
steps: Use a real calendar to count the days in several different months, including February, and record what you find: months have 28, 29 (February in a leap year), 30 or 31 days.
State why 'about 4 weeks in a month' is an approximation, not an exact conversion.
Contrast the exact fact (1 week = 7 days) with the approximate month fact, and explain how you would convert months to days versus weeks to days.
activities.insight: Some time units convert by exact fixed rates (7 days per week, 60 seconds per minute, 12 months per year) while month LENGTHS are irregular, so 'a month ≈ 4 weeks' cannot be used as an exact conversion to days.

activities.title: Pose-and-solve conversion word problems
steps: Read or hear a word problem (e.g. 'A film lasts 150 seconds — how long is that in minutes and seconds?') and solve it, saying each step aloud.
Explain for each problem which rate you used (×60, ×7, ×12) and how you handled any remainder or second unit.
activities.insight: Conversions apply in context; choosing the right rate and correctly expressing mixed/remainder answers is part of solving the problem.

checkQuestion: Set conversion problems and WATCH the method: (1) 'Change 3 hours 25 minutes into minutes — show me how.' (2) 'A programme lasts 150 seconds — write that in minutes and seconds.' (3) 'How many days are in 8 weeks and 3 days?' Watch whether they multiply by the right rate (x60, x7) and handle the remainder, or add up, assume base-10 (100 to a minute), or drop the mixed part.
checkAnswer: 3 x 60 = 180, + 25 = 205 minutes; 150 ÷ 60 = 2 remainder 30 -> 2 minutes 30 seconds; 8 x 7 = 56, + 3 = 59 days — using multiplicative reasoning and correctly combining the mixed parts.
